key_insight: Constitutive Kolmogorov-Arnold networks learn hyperelastic behavior from heterogeneous experiments and yield compact, closed-form strain-energy functions through pruning and symbolic regression.
engineering_relevance: The approach reduces reliance on hand-selected constitutive laws and multiple homogeneous tests while producing interpretable material models for finite element simulation.
method: Embed a constitutive Kolmogorov-Arnold network in finite element model updating.
Fit measured displacement fields and reaction forces.
Prune and symbolically regress the network into a constitutively admissible strain-energy function.
evidence_signal: Natural-rubber tests achieved median displacement errors of 1–2% and transfer to a withheld hole pattern; additional demonstrations covered silicone calibration from one load and anisotropic aortic inflation.
watch_item: Generalization beyond the tested geometries and loading regimes remains to be established.
paper_title: Constitutive Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks in Finite Element Model Updating: Closed-Form Hyperelastic Strain Energies from Heterogeneous Experiments
